answer:
## Direct answer

**Casual leave cannot be encashed at all**, so the "encash 2 days" step in your question is not permitted by the policy. Taking 3 days from a 14-day balance leaves **11 days** (14 − 3 = 11).

## How the balance is calculated

**Accrual and usage** [leave_policy § 3.1 Accrual and Usage]:
- Casual leave accrues at **1 day per completed month of service, up to 12 days per calendar year**.
- The balance is visible in the HRMS at the start of each month.
- You may use leave as soon as it has accrued; **advancing usage against future accrual is not permitted** — so the balance can never go negative.
- Probationary employees are limited to 1 casual leave day per month [leave_policy § 1. Overview].

**Deduction:** each approved casual leave day simply reduces the accrued balance by one day. The policy states no other formula, multiplier or deduction rule for casual leave.

**Your 14-day starting figure:** the annual entitlement is 12 days [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements], so a 14-day balance must include carried-forward days — 14 − 12 = 2 days carried in from the prior year. That is consistent with the carry-forward rules below.

## Encashment — the part that does not apply to casual leave

- **Casual leave:** any unused balance above the carry-forward cap "lapses permanently on December 31 and **cannot be recovered, encashed, or transferred to another leave type**" [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward].
- **Encashment exists only for Earned/Privilege Leave:** "Up to 5 unused days may be encashed at year end" [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements].

So if you want to encash 2 days, that has to come out of your Earned/Privilege Leave balance (18 days/year, 1.5 days per month, max 5 encashed at year end) — it cannot be taken from casual leave, and it does not reduce your casual leave balance.

## Carry-forward cap (relevant to the 14-day balance)

- The base policy caps carry-forward at **6 days**, with anything above lapsing on December 31 [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward].
- **The 2025 amendment supersedes this:** effective July 1, 2025, the cap is increased from 6 to **15 days**; any balance above 15 lapses on December 31, and carry-forward is applied automatically in the first payroll cycle of January [leave_policy_2025_amendment § Leave Policy Amendment — 2025 (Policy CL-2025-07)].

Under the amended 15-day cap, a 14-day balance would carry forward in full.

## Summary of the arithmetic

| Step | Days |
|---|---|
| Starting balance (given) | 14 |
| Less 3 days taken | −3 |
| **Remaining casual leave** | **11** (14 − 3) |
| Encash 2 days from casual leave | **Not permitted** — casual leave cannot be encashed |

Sources:
- [leave_policy § 3.1 Accrual and Usage]
- [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward]
- [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements]
- [leave_policy § 1. Overview]
- [leave_policy_2025_amendment § Leave Policy Amendment — 2025 (Policy CL-2025-07)]
